tagline: East from the outfitting town, where the wagons went first.
intro: East out of Lexington, US 24 runs through the little town of Dover to Waverly. The wagons came this way first. Once it had crossed the Missouri near Arrow Rock, the Santa Fe Trail ran roughly where US 24 runs now, through Lexington on its way to Fort Osage and Independence.

Lexington was the outfitting town, the largest city west of St. Louis in the 1830s and 1840s, where trappers, traders and emigrants got ready for the trails west. Hemp grew on the farms around it, and the hemp was made into rope.

moments.title: Lexington
moments.text: In the 1840s the freighters Russell, Majors and Waddell set up headquarters on Main Street, and Russell and Waddell went on to found the Pony Express.

moments.title: Dover
moments.text: Dover took its name from a church nearby and had a post office by that name in 1835, four years before anybody platted the town.

moments.title: Waverly
moments.text: Jo Shelby, a Kentucky ropemaker, came to Waverly to run steamboats, a hemp plantation, a ropeworks and a sawmill, and in 1861 he rode off with a company of Lafayette County mounted rifles.
